titleZh: 修好一件小东西，改变一种消费习惯

cet4.title: Giving Old Things a Second Life
cet4.summary: 灯坏了，人们通常会考虑换新，但也可以先查找故障。松动连接或零件损坏可能能够修复，调查原因会改变我们看待日常物品的方式。

paragraphs.text: A lamp stops working, and its owner begins to look for a new one. This is an ordinary response in a world where replacement is often easy. But another possibility exists: finding out what went wrong. A loose connection or a damaged part may be repairable. Choosing to investigate can change how people think about objects that have become part of their daily lives.
paragraphs.translation: 灯坏了，人们通常会考虑换新，但也可以先查找故障。松动连接或零件损坏可能能够修复，调查原因会改变我们看待日常物品的方式。

paragraphs.text: A community repair event offers a place to learn. Visitors bring broken items, and volunteers help examine them. The aim is not to promise that everything can be fixed. Some products are unsafe or too badly damaged. Instead, the event encourages questions. Watching a careful repair can help an owner understand what a product contains and why a small failure has stopped it from working.
paragraphs.translation: 社区维修活动让居民与志愿者共同检查物品。它并不保证修好所有东西，而是通过提问和观察帮助人们理解产品结构、故障及维修边界。

paragraphs.text: Repair also depends on design. If a case cannot be opened, or a replacement part is unavailable, even a skilled person may struggle. Instructions and suitable tools make a difference. Price matters as well: a repair that costs more than a new product is a difficult choice for many households. Asking individuals to reduce waste is only part of the answer when products are not designed to last.
paragraphs.translation: 维修受设计、零件、工具、说明及价格影响。当产品难以拆开或维修比换新还贵时，不能只要求个人凭热情减少浪费。

paragraphs.text: Not everyone needs to become an expert. Knowing when to ask for professional help is an important skill, especially with electrical equipment. Yet learning a simple repair can build confidence and patience. It may also make people consider durability before their next purchase. An object with a longer life offers more than saved money. It can remind its owner that care sometimes matters more than constant replacement.
paragraphs.translation: 人们无需成为专家，知道何时寻求专业帮助也很重要。简单维修能培养信心与耐心，并让人在下次购买时重视耐用性与照料。

paragraphs.text: Keeping a small record of maintenance can help too. A note about a replaced part or a previous fault gives the next repairer a useful starting point. Passing that information to a new owner can extend the benefit beyond one household. Looking after an object includes looking after the knowledge that keeps it useful.
paragraphs.translation: 记录曾更换的零件和故障，可以帮助之后的维修者。转交物品时也传递这些知识，能让维护经验持续发挥作用。

focusWords.contextMeaning: 指物品损坏后直接用新物品替换，而非先考虑维修。

examples.text: The old chair is beyond repair and needs replacement.
examples.translation: 那把旧椅子已经无法修理，需要更换。

examples.text: Replacement of the damaged part took only a few minutes.
examples.translation: 更换损坏的部件只花了几分钟。

focusWords.contextMeaning: 指产品能够长期使用的品质，是购买前可以考虑的因素。

examples.text: We chose the table for its durability rather than its fashionable colour.
examples.translation: 我们选择这张桌子是因为它耐用，而不是颜色时髦。

examples.text: The durability of the fabric matters for everyday work clothes.
examples.translation: 对于日常工作服来说，面料的耐用性很重要。

focusWords.contextMeaning: 指记录更换部件、旧故障等日常维护信息，帮助后续维修。

examples.text: Regular maintenance keeps the bicycle in good condition.
examples.translation: 定期保养能让自行车保持良好状态。

examples.text: The school keeps a maintenance record for every piece of equipment.
examples.translation: 学校为每件设备保存维护记录。

questions.prompt: What does repair culture encourage people to consider?
options: The idea that broken items never have value.
The continuing usefulness of objects.
Only the newest product advertisement.
The belief that every repair is safe.
questions.explanation: 维修文化重视长期使用价值和已有投入。

questions.prompt: What is a realistic aim of a community repair event?
options: Helping people understand problems and possible solutions.
Guaranteeing that every item will be repaired.
Replacing all professional repair services.
Teaching people to ignore safety concerns.
questions.explanation: 活动强调调查、理解与安全边界，并非保证全部修好。

questions.prompt: Which factor can make repair difficult?
options: Clear and usable instructions.
An object that can be opened safely.
The availability of appropriate tools.
A lack of accessible spare parts.
questions.explanation: 缺少备件会限制维修，其他选项通常有助于维修。

questions.prompt: What should people do when a repair could be unsafe?
options: Assume every online suggestion is reliable.
Ask an inexperienced child to take over.
Seek help from a qualified professional.
Continue regardless of the danger.
questions.explanation: 文章强调知道何时需要专业帮助。

questions.prompt: What change in purchasing decisions does the author support?
options: Avoiding questions about product design.
Giving more attention to durability and repairability.
Always choosing a product because it looks new.
Ignoring future maintenance costs.
questions.explanation: 关注耐用性和可维修性，是维修思维在购买前的延伸。

cet6.title: Repair Culture and the Meaning of Product Value
cet6.summary: 灯坏了，人们通常会考虑换新，但也可以先查找故障。松动连接或零件损坏可能能够修复，调查原因会改变我们看待日常物品的方式。

paragraphs.text: When a familiar household object fails, replacement can seem like the most natural response. New products are visible, convenient and often heavily promoted, whereas the possibility of repair may be difficult to assess. This imbalance affects how value is understood. The purchase price becomes highly visible, while the future costs of maintenance and disposal receive less attention. Repair culture invites consumers to extend that perspective and ask what makes a product useful over time.
paragraphs.translation: 换新显得方便自然，但这让购买价格与新奇性更突出，而维护和处置成本容易被忽略。维修文化促使人们从长期使用角度理解价值。

paragraphs.text: Community repair events make this question practical. By bringing owners and experienced volunteers together, they turn a private inconvenience into an opportunity for shared learning. A successful event does not guarantee that every object will be restored. Rather, it allows people to investigate failure, understand possible remedies and recognise the limits of safe intervention. Observing the process may be as valuable as taking a functioning item home, because it builds knowledge that can inform future choices.
paragraphs.translation: 社区维修把私人烦恼转为共同学习机会。活动不保证恢复所有物品，而是帮助居民了解故障、补救方式和安全边界，这些知识能影响未来选择。

paragraphs.text: However, a culture of care cannot compensate for every design decision. Products that are difficult to open, contain permanently attached components or lack accessible spare parts restrict what even knowledgeable repairers can achieve. Availability of instructions and tools therefore matters. So does the economic context. For a household with limited income, a technically possible repair may remain unrealistic if it costs substantially more than replacement. Environmental appeals should acknowledge these constraints rather than placing the entire responsibility on individual motivation.
paragraphs.translation: 照料无法弥补所有设计缺陷。不可拆卸结构、缺少备件和说明会限制维修。经济约束也真实存在，环保诉求应承认条件限制。

paragraphs.text: There is also a distinction between encouraging learning and encouraging unsafe experimentation. Electrical equipment, batteries and other specialised products may require professional assessment. A responsible approach includes knowing when to stop and seek qualified assistance. Repair events can communicate this boundary while still offering accessible tasks through which participants develop confidence. The objective is informed participation, not the expectation that every consumer must become an engineer or perform every repair independently.
paragraphs.translation: 鼓励学习不等于鼓励危险试验。电气设备、电池等可能需要专业评估；负责任的参与包括知道何时停止、何时求助。

paragraphs.text: In the longer term, repairability can influence decisions made before an object is purchased. Consumers may ask whether components can be replaced, whether guidance will remain available and whether the product suits a durable pattern of use. These questions move attention from novelty towards continuing usefulness. Repair is therefore not merely an activity that follows failure. It can become a way of evaluating design, organising local knowledge and recognising the time and resources already invested in the objects around us.
paragraphs.translation: 可维修性还能影响购买前的判断。零部件替换、长期指导和持续适用性，让人们从新奇转向长期价值，也重视物品中已有的资源投入。

paragraphs.text: Practical knowledge can also be preserved alongside the object itself. A record of previous faults, replacement components and relevant instructions gives a future repairer a better starting point. If an item changes hands, transferring that record can prevent useful experience from being lost. Maintenance is therefore partly an informational practice: keeping something useful may depend on keeping the knowledge required to understand it. This gives households another modest way to support a longer product life.
paragraphs.translation: 故障、零件与说明等记录，是未来维修的起点。物品转手时传递记录能保留经验，因此维护也包含保存让物品持续可用的信息。

focusWords.contextMeaning: 指维修活动中针对物品故障寻找的可行解决办法。

examples.text: The report identifies the fault and suggests several remedies.
examples.translation: 报告找出了故障，并提出了几种补救办法。

examples.text: We should examine the cause before choosing a remedy for the problem.
examples.translation: 我们应先检查原因，再选择解决问题的办法。

focusWords.contextMeaning: 指收入、维修成本和产品设计等限制，不能只要求消费者有环保意愿。

examples.text: A small team must work within clear budget constraints.
examples.translation: 小团队必须在明确的预算限制内开展工作。

examples.text: Time constraints prevented us from testing every possible design.
examples.translation: 时间限制使我们无法测试每一种可能的设计。

focusWords.contextMeaning: 指产品适合长期、持续使用，而非只追求新鲜感。

examples.text: Choose a durable bag that can withstand daily use.
examples.translation: 选一个经得住日常使用的耐用包。

examples.text: The repairer recommended a more durable replacement part.
examples.translation: 维修人员推荐了一个更耐用的替换部件。
